revisions.title: Education teaches the pleasure of the beautiful
revisions.body: The Athenian defines education through choral practice: song and dance are its parts, but bodily performance is not enough. The sharper criterion is whether pleasure and dislike are correctly trained toward the beautiful and shameful; the exchange then compresses this provisional account to keep the inquiry moving.

revisions.title: A persuasive myth becomes an age-ranked chorus
revisions.body: The Sidonian story is marked as improbable but useful as a paradigm for legislation. From that persuasive example the Athenian orders participation by age: children and younger adults sing in distinct choruses, while older men are assigned myth-telling and a Dionysian chorus; wine is introduced as the device that makes elder participation in song practicable.
